utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Josse, are you ready to continue the examination of Witness D14?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we have to go into private session? I think we finished in private session last Friday, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We did finish in private session. We don't need to begin in private session, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Could the witness have the bundle, please. Could the witness turn to tab 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: If you look, D14, at the first chart that appears in that bundle, are any of the names of the individuals that appear in that chart familiar to you, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Which names are familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We can't hear the witness. We cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Witness, could you stop, please. It's my fault. Could I ask you to begin again and read out which names are familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Josse, before we continue, is this tab 4 document related to the tab 3 document? That's in my mind. That's also what I could imagine on the basis of some writing at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, it is. There's no secret about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please first clarify what this is, who drafted it, unless you just want these names.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, I was going to attempt to deal with this in a slightly different fashion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. But you are aware of my concern at this moment and the concern of the Chamber. Please proceed and Mr. Harmon will certainly -- it's always a bit difficult if I invite you to explain exactly; that might not be the proper thing to do in the presence of the witness. At the same time, you're now aware of my concern.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would invite the Court to go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Do you accept, Witness, in 1992 by the end of summer and the beginning of autumn there was a large movement of non-Serb population from Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have to say that the initial request came at the beginning of summer, the beginning of June, and there was some smaller group that left already as early as that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Why did you understand that these people were leaving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are several reasons in my mind. One of the reasons was the fact that the Croat population of Kotor Varos had some -- somebody that worked abroad in every family. And since the living conditions were getting harder and more and more uncertain, for that reason it was better for him to go to the areas where there were more supplies, where it was easier to provide for one's family. On the other hand, combat activities had already started in the territory of Kotor Varos municipality. The town itself was encircled, and the places surrounding Kotor Varos belonged to Croats or Muslims because the majority population there was either Croat or Muslim. In those places, there were armed formations, at the time paramilitary formations. And since negotiations were in place for them to surrender their weapons and those negotiations were only partly successful, what I'm saying is that from some places the weapons were returned, but from the others they weren't. And from the latter, there was sniper fire, there was mortar fire, even the hotel in the centre of town was hit by a rocket launcher. For all those reasons, I believe that people did not feel safe, and that was the second reason why they left. Also, I think that there were also certain requests for some people to be moved out because we had a situation. Once when the war was already finished in 1995, from a Croatian place called Zabrdje, a lot of Croats moved out that had stayed there throughout the war. Their houses were intact, they were not damaged. We believed that they were invited to leave the municipality of Kotor Varos because of the things that were happening in Croatia in 1995. Let me conclude. I believe that those were misfortunate people who left the area for various reasons. They personally filed requests to do that. It was their desire to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Witness, please turn in the bundle to tab 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I appreciate and apologise for the fact that all these documents presently, Your Honour, are untranslated, but I think I'm going to be able to assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Am I right, Witness, that what chart -- tab 7 is relates to criminal charges filed by the military police to the military prosecutor's office dated the 13th of September, 1993, against four individuals for breaking into the flat of a person and taking away money in various currencies and other values?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, four persons are involved. The military prosecutor of the military court in Banja Luka received a report, a criminal report, in 1993 for the crimes that were committed on the 11th of September, 1993, in the apartment belonging to Zdenka Abazic. At gunpoint, her husband said -- was forced to give these persons 2.000 German marks, 1.300 Austrian shillings, 192 American dollars, 150 Swiss francs, one player, one synthesiser, and two swords.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Are you able to help us with the ethnicity, firstly, of Zdenka Abazic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either Bosniak, Muslim that is, or Croat. And Sead, her husband, is a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: What about the alleged perpetrators of this crime? There are four of them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The four of them are Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Have you any idea what happened to the allegation against these four Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Could that have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab 7, Your Honours, would be D127.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness D14, could you tell us if you have similar examples of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that there were criminal reports of that sort.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean do you have any document on 1992 which gives us a similar insight on proceedings or at least reports brought against suspects?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document was issued on the 28th of June, 1992. Again, there are four Serb perpetrators involved. They committed, according to this allegation, rapes of several non-Serb women --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Can I stop you, Witness? Can I stop you. This is tab 9. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I was going to turn to this, Your Honour, but we're now going to -- I didn't want to interrupt Your Honour's question. Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but under "criminal charges" does it say what the profession of the perpetrators is? If I have understood things correctly, it contains the date of birth, place of birth perhaps, but is there anything that indicates what their profession is?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'm just having that checked. Perhaps again we can clarify one matter. As we go along we will answer Your Honour's question, if we may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we perhaps we first -- I take it that you want that exhibited as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: May I suggest we go to tab 8 next.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Because tab 8, Witness, is in fact the proposed indictment in relation to the offenders mentioned in tab 7. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And is it right that if we look at tab 8 it mentions the occupation of the alleged perpetrators of this crime?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, and their marital status. And in document under tab 9, there is something important --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Stop. Stop, please. We'll come to tab 9 in a moment. Tell the learned Judge the occupation of each of the men in tab 8. Give their name and give their occupation, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Witness, you gave us some evidence yesterday about the events in Kotor Varos relating to World War II which generated fear among the Serb population, and then you also related having seen refugees. Can you tell us what it was about those refugees that made an impact on you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had a feeling that they had been forced to leave their houses, that they did it in a haste. They mostly travelled in horse-carts and in tractors. In some cases, they had a few trailers. They had things covered by pieces of nylon or tarpaulin. They were mostly elderly people, elderly men, women, and children. It was the first time for me to see any refugees. Before that, I only saw them in movies and I always thought that this was part of the set and just part of the feature movie for people to watch. But then I realised that this was a sad reality for those people and that they had been forced to leave their households.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Were you affected in any way by their lack of material resources?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their things were scattered all over, and most of the women and children were crying, in a disheveled state. And it was difficult for me to see anybody in such a condition. And, as I've already said, this was the first time for me to see any refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Did it appear to you that they had with them material resources sufficient to take care of their needs, their future needs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D14 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their possessions were mostly covered by nylons, tarpaulins. I don't know what they had, but it seemed to me that they had just the bare necessities, that they only had what they could get hold of, that they could grab in a haste.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think this is an appropriate time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's close to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I want to deal with one very short matter in the absence of the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then let's ask Madam Usher to escort the witness out of the courtroom. But, Witness D14 -- first of all the technicians are instructed not to show the face of the witness when leaving the courtroom. First, I would like to instruct you not to speak with anyone about the testimony you have given and still are to give and would like to see you back tomorrow - we are not sitting in the morning but we are sitting in the afternoon - in this same courtroom at a quarter past 2.00. Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Josse, I think we're still in open session. We are, yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I don't expect an answer to this from Prosecution immediately, but I'd like to inquire formally whether P1045 has ever been served on the Defence under Rule 68. That's my only matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, I take it that you'll be able to check that --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Quite quickly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Quite quickly, Your Honour. And Your Honours had asked for the exhibit numbers of those previous cases. I don't know if I had given them to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: They're P202 and P203.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then finally, if we're talking about numbers anyhow, where referring to sacrosanct words I immediately made a mistake where I said P1046 and 1043 were admitted into evidence because the exhibits admitted to evidence are P1043 up to and including P1043. That has been -- now I made a mistake again. It's P1036 up to and including P1043. I apologise for the mistake. We stand adjourned until quarter past 2.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 24th day of January, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.50 p.m.,
